doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Jaco Pastorius and the Japan tour
title: The Tokyo and Yokohama concerts
summary: In Japan the Jaco band, Herman and Kai Winding groups met for a concert; Jaco arrived in war paint.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: He always started out, like we had this party in Tokyo when we first got there and Woody Herman was there with Flip Phillips and Al Cohn and I don’t know if Zoot was there. All-star Woody Herman band or some pick-up band. And Kai Winding was there with J.J. Johnson. It was a big thing in Japan where we all came together at the end in Yokohama and put on this huge concert. But after this feast, it was a feast, we all went our separate ways on the road so to speak in Japan, and then we all met at the end of about a week’s time in Yokohama and put on this big concert. So sure enough everybody’s seated down and everybody’s like it was very formal too, speeches and everything else, so Jaco comes in after everybody is sat down, I think after it even started, he’s like dressed in Indian war paint with a band around his head. And Woody Herman said to me, milling around the sushi and everything else after the speeches, Woody says, “Who in the hell is this guy you’re with?” I don’t think Woody knew him. I don’t know if he knew of him from before with the Weather Report or not, I don’t know, but he was adored, as well he should have been musically, by the people in Japan. He could do no wrong.
